title: Graphs of functions
text: Look at the symmetry of the graph. Odd functions have rotational symmetry about the origin.\n##figure1.gif##

figureAlts.figure1.gif:
Three graphs of inverse trigonometric functions drawn in blue, arranged in two rows. In all cases, the horizontal axis is x, and the vertical axis is theta. Top left: theta equals arcsine of x. The curve is strictly increasing on a closed domain from x equals negative one to x equals positive one. It starts at the point negative one comma negative pi over two; passes through the origin; and ends at the point one comma pi over two.
Top right: theta equals arccosine of x. The curve is strictly decreasing on a closed domain from x equals negative one to x equals positive one. It starts at the point negative one comma pi; passes through the point zero comma pi over two; and ends at the point one comma zero.
Bottom row, full width: theta equals arctangent of x. The curve is strictly increasing for all real numbers. It passes through the origin and approaches horizontal dashed-line asymptotes at theta equals pi over two and theta equals negative pi over two.
